title: A Man Who Keeps Moving
summary: Open on Brandon as an ordinary drifter crossing the Sunfields in Jessie's battered rig. The narrator establishes the simple truth of who he is before anyone else gets a chance to rename him.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE HORIZONTAL, roughly the upper third. Hard white Sunfields under a huge pale sky; Jessie's battered rig is tiny on the road. A half-buried black Sunforge rib sits well off the shoulder with two travelers using it as shade. Leave clean sky for the two opening caption boxes; the image should feel hot and ordinary, not ominous.

Panel 2 — MEDIUM TWO-SHOT inside the moving rig from low passenger-side eye level. Brandon sits loose but alert with one boot braced, hat low and satchel at his feet; Jessie drives in profile. Jessie identifies the Last Drop and Brandon answers without turning toward her.

Panel 3 — TIGHTER PROFILE on Jessie, one hand on the wheel, goggles pushed up. Through the windshield the heat shimmer is beginning to resolve into buildings. Her dry correction about the water lands here; Brandon's reply can come from off-panel.

Panel 4 — NARROW BOTTOM WIDE. The rig approaches a hand-painted roadside board: LAST DROP — WATER / SHADE / ROOMS. Keep the travelers small and the road dominant; this is a quiet page-ending destination beat.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not because anybody ran him out of anywhere. He just tends to keep moving.

directionInline.text: Establish the narrator immediately as dry, factual and slightly amused. It may know ordinary facts about people but does not know or explain the larger mystery. Do not make the opening ominous.

title: One Drink
summary: Jessie drops Brandon at the Last Drop for water and food. Their existing arrangement is casual enough that neither calls it companionship yet, but Jessie expects him back at the rig.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE ESTABLISHING across the top. The rig rolls into the Last Drop: patched roofs, hitching rails, shade cloth, a water trough and people doing ordinary midday work. The saloon is the darkest opening in the street. First Jessie caption sits over the town rather than over a character close-up.

Panel 2 — MEDIUM inside the stopped rig. Brandon lifts his satchel, then hesitates and leaves it on the floor. Use the second caption here; their temporary arrangement should be visible before either character admits one exists.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM from outside the passenger side. Brandon has stepped down into the glare. Jessie calls his name from the driver's seat; he turns back with a simple 'What?'

Panel 4 — TWO-SHOT across the open passenger doorway. Jessie gives him the food/water/ten-minute instruction; Brandon answers about being timed and offending the sun. Keep the acting casual, practiced and mildly amused.

Panel 5 — INSERT/DETAIL on Jessie's hand nudging Brandon's satchel deeper into the rig with two fingers. Her 'Leave the bag' exchange with Brandon belongs here; the gesture should do more relationship work than the words.

Panel 6 — MEDIUM-LONG from behind Brandon as he heads for the saloon. Jessie has already faced forward again. Brandon calls the presumptuous remark back over his shoulder; Jessie answers only 'Ten minutes.'

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: JESSIE PETRESCU gave him a ride yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither of them has discussed whether that arrangement is still in effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'll try not to offend it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Because then you'll come back for it.

directionInline.text: Their chemistry should already have mild friction and familiarity, but not intimacy. Jessie is practical, not possessive; Brandon is amused enough not to argue about the bag.

title: Nothing Ever Happens Here
summary: Meet Eva as a bored sixteen-year-old embedded in the Last Drop's ordinary social life. She notices the scarred patron react when Jessie calls Brandon's name from outside, before Brandon himself has done anything interesting.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE INTERIOR establishing the Last Drop before Brandon enters. Dim patched bar, card table, flies at a bright window, lunch plates, boots on chairs. Eva wipes the same patch of bar while the bartender counts coins. Both Eva captions live in the quieter upper area of the panel.

Panel 2 — MEDIUM on Eva and the bartender. Eva glances toward the doorway, bored enough to watch any traveler pass, then back to the room. Carry the religious-practice / charge-admission exchange here and let the bartender remain busy rather than performing for her.

Panel 3 — OVER THE SCARRED PATRON'S SHOULDER toward the open door. His cup pauses halfway to his mouth as Jessie's distant 'Brandon' carries in from outside. Do not make the reaction supernatural; it is the small physical hitch of somebody hearing a familiar-sounding name.

Panel 4 — DOORWAY COMPOSITION. Brandon's silhouette crosses from white glare into the dark room. The patron studies his face, uncertainty turning into recognition because he now has both a near-name and a resemblance.
Panel 5 — CLOSE on Eva noticing the patron rather than Brandon. Her boredom is gone. The first real event of her day is somebody else's reaction.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: She has spent most of the summer waiting for something to happen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: If I wipe this spot again, I think it becomes a religious practice.

directionInline.text: Eva belongs to the place before she leaves it. Give the Last Drop ordinary rhythms and familiar faces. The patron's reaction begins with a plausible mishearing, not a planted message or supernatural recognition.

title: Brannock
summary: The scarred patron has heard Jessie say 'Brandon' through the noise and taken it for 'Brannock.' Brandon resembles the local Brannock closely enough that the mistake hardens into certainty before anyone can correct it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE TOP PANEL. Brandon stands just inside the doorway, still adjusting to the dim room; the scarred patron rises in the foreground. The patron says 'Brannock.' Place 'Jessie said BRANDON.' as a caption that lets the reader understand the mistake before Brandon does.

Panel 2 — TIGHT CLOSE-UP on the patron's face, pale cheek scar prominent but natural. 'The man at the wall heard BRANNOCK.' and the short Brannock-history caption belong here. His certainty should be social and emotional, not mystical.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM on Brandon looking back over his shoulder toward the empty doorway, genuinely checking whether the name was meant for somebody else. He gives the polite wrong-man correction.
Panel 4 — REVERSE TWO-SHOT with the patron foreground and Brandon beyond. 'Don't smile at me.' / 'I wasn't.' Let Brandon's expression support the answer: confused, not cocky.

Panel 5 — WIDER ROOM REACTION. Eva has stopped wiping; several locals are now looking over. The final Brandon-Mack captions sit over the room while the patron's hand closes around his bottle in the lower foreground, setting up the next page.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The man at the wall heard BRANNOCK.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Depending on who tells it around the Last Drop, Brannock was a thief, a killer, a hero, or all three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm sorry. You've got the wrong man.

directionInline.text: The first false identity is genuinely accidental. The near-name plus a rough resemblance and an existing local legend are enough for confirmation bias to take over. This is not one of Raina or Samuel's setups.

title: A Bottle
summary: The patron throws a bottle and then himself. Brandon reacts efficiently without turning the room into a showdown; Eva's curiosity becomes personal because Brandon refuses to behave like the returning outlaw everyone expects.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — DIAGONAL ACTION PANEL. The scarred patron throws the bottle as he accuses Brandon of being remembered; Brandon starts to slip aside while answering that the man does not know him. Keep both bodies readable.
Panel 2 — SMALL IMPACT INSET. Glass explodes against the doorframe where Brandon's head was. Nearby patrons recoil; nobody draws yet.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM ACTION. The patron lunges through the broken-glass aftermath, insisting on the same face. Brandon catches wrist and shoulder rather than punching him.

Panel 4 — WIDE HORIZONTAL. Brandon uses the man's momentum to fold him chest-down across an empty table. Cups jump but do not spill. Brandon's dry line about that being the problem lands during the restraint, not as a victory pose.
Panel 5 — REACTION PANEL on Eva, rag still in one hand, now several steps closer than she was. She asks whether Brandon knows the man.

Panel 6 — MEDIUM AFTERMATH. Brandon releases the patron immediately and steps back, hands open. He looks to Eva for the first time when he says he was hoping she knew. The room stays tense around them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scarred patron
dialogueInline.text: You think I don't remember you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I think you don't know me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That does seem to be the problem.

directionInline.text: No martial-arts flourish. Brandon's physical competence is practical and proportionate. Eva should be intrigued by the mismatch between the room's expectation and Brandon's behavior.

title: The Darkest Table
summary: Brandon ends the confrontation by sitting down rather than claiming the room. Eva brings him water and invites herself into the empty chair opposite.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE AFTERMATH across the room. The scarred patron remains bent over the table catching his breath in the foreground while Brandon quietly rights the chair he knocked aside. Other patrons are watching for a second act that does not come; one person cautiously resumes eating.

Panel 2 — MEDIUM TRACKING VIEW as Brandon crosses toward the darkest back table instead of claiming the center of the room. Without stopping, he asks the bartender for water; the bartender's question about buying something comes from behind the bar.

Panel 3 — CLOSE TABLE DETAIL. Brandon sits, removes his gloves and places them beside his hands. A chipped cup enters frame. His 'If you have food' answer belongs here; the physical decompression after the fight is the beat.

Panel 4 — OVER EVA'S SHOULDER as she sets down the cup and hooks the empty chair out with one foot. She offers 'Water or explanation?' Brandon chooses water. Keep the room visible beyond him so this does not become an isolated talking-head shot.

Panel 5 — LARGER BOTTOM PANEL, relaxed two-shot with depth. Brandon drinks half the cup before finally looking at Eva; she sits without invitation. Behind them, the room starts moving again while still watching. Eva admits she has no explanation; Brandon's 'That worked out' closes the page.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Could I get some water, please?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Good, because I don't have the explanation.

directionInline.text: Let the room remain active around them. Background locals whisper, resume eating, or keep watching. The story does not freeze into a two-shot just because Eva sits down.

title: Problems He Understands
summary: Eva tries to turn the encounter into a mystery. Brandon is more interested in water and lunch, and accidentally reveals just enough guardedness to make Eva more curious.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM TABLE TWO-SHOT. A plate of bread, beans and fried food lands between them as Eva says the patron knew Brandon's face. Brandon answers while reaching for the food, putting lunch ahead of the mystery.
Panel 2 — TIGHTER on Eva leaning forward as Brandon takes a first bite. She asks if he is curious. His longer answer about already-understood problems gets enough quiet space to land.
Panel 3 — OVER BRANDON'S SHOULDER toward the scarred patron whispering with another local. Brandon glances over despite himself; Eva catches the glance from the edge of frame.
Panel 4 — CLOSE TWO-SHOT. Eva immediately asks what kind of problems. Brandon realizes he opened the door farther than intended: 'Bah. Leave it alone...' Let his annoyance be mostly with himself.
Panel 5 — SMALL REACTION on Eva, pleased because she knows she got something real. 'You absolutely did.'

Panel 6 — WIDER BOTTOM PANEL. Brandon returns deliberately to his plate and makes lunch the subject again; Eva stays opposite, unconvinced. Their final three lines play over ordinary eating rather than dramatic posing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: He knew a face. Mine happened to be standing there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I've got enough problems I already understand, I don't much care about ones I don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Bah. Leave it alone. I didn't mean anything by that.

directionInline.text: Protect the approved Brandon voice. He is conversational and grammatical, not cryptic. His accidental self-disclosure and retreat should feel like a natural boundary, not a mystery tease.

title: The Story Starts Moving
summary: While Brandon eats, the room begins converting the encounter into a Brannock story in real time. Eva hears contradictions accumulate and realizes Brandon's indifference is not stopping the narrative from growing around him.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE ROOM SLICE showing the scarred patron retelling the encounter to two locals while Brandon and Eva remain visible far in the background. The gray-hair disagreement begins here; make the rumor physically separate from Brandon.

Panel 2 — SECOND GOSSIP ANGLE at another table. A local insists Brannock was taller; the scarred patron corrects him with 'You're thinking of Rusk.' The story is already branching through people who are not talking to Brandon.

Panel 3 — MEDIUM at Brandon's table. Eva listens to both conversations at once while Brandon tears bread into his beans. She says they are already disagreeing about him; his 'That seems healthy' is genuinely dry, not a punchline pose.
Panel 4 — BAR-SIDE ANGLE. The bartender sets down a refill and quietly offers the back door. Brandon answers that he has not finished eating. Keep the exit visible behind him.
Panel 5 — CLOSE TWO-SHOT. Eva calls out his commitment to lunch; Brandon looks at the plate when he says it has not accused him of anything.
Panel 6 — DOORWAY REVEAL at the bottom of the page. Jessie stands in the bright entrance carrying Brandon's satchel, taking in the room before speaking on the next page.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Brannock had gray in his hair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You are remarkably committed to lunch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It hasn't accused me of anything.

directionInline.text: This page dramatizes social mutation rather than explaining it. Different locals should have different memories and motives. End on Jessie's arrival as the page turn into the travel relationship.

title: Too Hot Here
summary: Jessie has read the town's social temperature from outside and brought Brandon's satchel. Her casual 'we' surprises him more than the warning itself; Eva immediately tries to join the arrangement.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE from inside the saloon toward the doorway. Jessie stands against the glare with Brandon's satchel over one shoulder; the scarred patron and other locals remain in the room behind Brandon. She says the place is too hot and uses 'we' for the first time.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM Brandon/Jessie. Brandon's surprise is at the word, not the warning: 'We?' / 'Yes.'
Panel 3 — TIGHTER TWO-SHOT with Eva watching from the edge. Brandon says there is no 'we'; Jessie simply reframes it as herself leaving and him being free to come. No romantic weight.
Panel 4 — WINDOW-SIDE COMPOSITION. Through the window, three locals are gathering near the rig and talking. Brandon admits that formulation is different; Jessie says not from where she is standing.
Panel 5 — MEDIUM on Eva rising with immediate commitment. She asks about herself; Jessie says she has not decided whether Eva is helping, and Eva answers for her. End on Jessie's dry reaction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It's too hot here for you. We're leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Fine. I'm leaving. You can come with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I haven't decided whether you're helping.

directionInline.text: Jessie reads people, not prophecy. Her use of 'we' is practical and slightly presumptuous. Eva should clock the relationship instantly and begin inserting herself into it.

title: What Jessie Saw
summary: Outside, Jessie explains the practical reason for leaving: people are beginning to gather around a story rather than an event. Eva interprets Jessie's readiness to leave as evidence that Jessie trusts Brandon more than she admits.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE EXTERIOR in punishing glare. Jessie walks straight toward the rig; Brandon follows adjusting the satchel. He asks what happened to ten minutes; Jessie says he used them.

Panel 2 — LONG-LENS STREET VIEW past Brandon toward the small knot of locals openly watching him. One points toward the back of the saloon. Eva notes Jessie had his bag ready; Jessie gives the concrete reason.
Panel 3 — MOVING THREE-SHOT. Eva walks backward in front of Jessie while Jessie keeps going. Eva says Jessie believes Brandon; Jessie answers that she believes what she has seen him do.

Panel 4 — CLOSE on Eva shifting her attention from Brandon to Jessie. 'That's a careful answer.' Jessie gives the reason for being careful. This is the first panel primarily about the two women rather than the mystery.

Panel 5 — MEDIUM-LONG with Brandon several steps behind, tying the satchel strap while clearly hearing them. He finally calls out that he can hear both of them. Eva does not turn around when she says, 'We know.'

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You had his bag before he agreed to go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: There were three men outside deciding whether they remembered him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I believe what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough for a careless one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I can hear both of you.

directionInline.text: This is the first real Eva/Jessie relationship scene. The subject is Brandon, but the deeper content is how each woman decides what she believes about a person.

title: Behind the Saloon
summary: The trio is almost out when noise behind the saloon draws Brandon around the corner. The issue turns from social inconvenience to immediate human danger.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM at the rig. Jessie crouches at the front wheel checking it while Eva hovers; Brandon approaches. Jessie says 'No' before he says anything. Brandon answers that he did not say anything.

Panel 2 — INSERT on the shadowed rear wall of the saloon: a dull wooden knock, rope creak and an ugly choking sound from off-panel. No faces. Jessie's answer about Brandon stopping walking comes across the sound beat.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM on Brandon frozen mid-step, head turned toward the back lot. Eva asks what is there; Brandon says he does not know yet.

Panel 4 — TRACKING VIEW as Brandon heads around the rear corner with Eva following. Jessie remains by the rig, eyes briefly closed in resignation. 'Brandon.' / 'One minute.' / 'That phrase is losing value.'
Panel 5 — TALL NARROW PAGE-TURN IMAGE from Brandon's viewpoint around the corner: only Tomas's boots and lower legs visible, kicking several inches above the dirt. No explanatory dialogue.

directionInline.text: Use the page turn. Do not reveal the full hanging until Page 12. Jessie's frustration is affectionate only in hindsight; right now it is practical recognition of Brandon's inability to ignore an immediate problem.

title: Dead Weight
summary: Reveal Tomas being publicly hanged in the back lot while Marcus and several locals watch. Brandon does not ask for the history before intervening.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE REVEAL occupying nearly half the page. Tomas hangs from a loading beam behind the saloon, boots scraping empty air; Marcus Kovacs and two locals stand nearby as if supervising routine punishment. Use the two narrator captions high in open space.
Panel 2 — CLOSE on Brandon's eyes and the geometry he is reading: rope, beam, barrel, Tomas's feet. Marcus says to leave him; Brandon answers that Tomas is still alive.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM Marcus turning toward Brandon, irritated rather than ashamed. 'Not for long.' Brandon is already moving past him when he asks for a hand.
Panel 4 — LOW ANGLE as Brandon drags the barrel under Tomas. The watching locals stay in frame; nobody helps yet.
Panel 5 — TIGHT PHYSICAL ACTION. Brandon climbs, shoulders Tomas's weight awkwardly and draws a knife to the rope. End on strain, not hero posing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Behind the Last Drop, Marcus Kovacs is hanging a man named Tomas.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brandon does not know Tomas either.

directionInline.text: The narrator supplies only facts. Brandon's action should precede any moral speech. He helps because a man is currently choking, not because he has diagnosed the town.

title: Cut the Rope
summary: Brandon cuts Tomas down while Marcus invokes Brannock again. Eva arrives in time to see Brandon prioritize Tomas over the accusation.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — TIGHT on Brandon's knife sawing through the rope while Tomas's weight drives both men off balance. Marcus answers Brandon's previous-page request for help with a flat 'No.' Brandon tells him to stay out of the way and keeps cutting.

Panel 2 — WIDE IMPACT. The rope parts and Brandon and Tomas crash into the dirt together. Marcus accuses Brandon of still giving orders; Brandon answers that he is trying to get Tomas down, not run the yard.

Panel 3 — GROUND-LEVEL CLOSE. Brandon rolls Tomas onto his side and works the noose loose while Marcus advances in the background: 'Same as Brannock. Walk in and decide what's right.' Brandon says he does not know Brannock.
Panel 4 — MEDIUM from Tomas's level as Eva rushes in around the corner carrying water. She calls to Brandon; he takes the cup without looking away from Tomas and tells her to go slow.

Panel 5 — CLOSE on Tomas finally coughing air. Marcus presses the identity accusation—asking whether Brandon really expects him to believe he does not remember him—while Brandon ignores the bait long enough to tell Tomas not to talk yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then stay out of the way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm trying to get him down.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Same as Brannock. Walk in and decide what's right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You really expect me to believe you don't remember me?

directionInline.text: Brandon can learn Tomas's name from somebody shouting it during the rescue or from Tomas himself in a rasp; keep that incidental. The important beat is that Brandon's attention remains on the present-tense person.

title: Marcus's Brannock
summary: Marcus tries to force Brandon into Brannock's old role by naming grievances and daring him to deny them. Brandon keeps refusing the premise and tending Tomas, which frustrates Marcus more than a duel would.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE YARD GEOMETRY. Marcus stands over the scene with the pipe low in one hand and says, 'I'm talking to you,' directly continuing his unanswered accusation from the prior page. Brandon, still beside Tomas, answers that he heard him.

Panel 2 — LOW MEDIUM on Brandon and Tomas while Eva gives water. Marcus finally states the grievance: Brandon supposedly burned his brother out of the Last Drop. Brandon says he has never been here before.
Panel 3 — CLOSE on Marcus demanding eye contact: 'Look me in the face and say that.' Brandon keeps watching Tomas and says he is trying to keep him breathing.
Panel 4 — MEDIUM as Marcus steps close enough to crowd Brandon physically. He orders Brandon to get up. Brandon stays where he is and answers, 'No, sir.'

Panel 5 — OVER EVA'S SHOULDER toward Marcus and the watching locals. Hold the silence after Brandon's refusal long enough for Marcus's humiliation to become public; his next move will open the following page.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You burned my brother out of this place.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Look me in the face and say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm trying to keep Tomas breathing.

directionInline.text: Marcus should not sound like he is delivering backstory for the reader. Give him personal anger and need for acknowledgment. Brandon's refusal deprives him of the scene he expected.

title: The Wrong Fight
summary: Marcus swings first. Brandon avoids him without escalating into a duel, and the conflict becomes visibly less about Brannock than Marcus's need to maintain control in front of the town.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — DYNAMIC DIAGONAL. Marcus swings the pipe immediately after Brandon's 'No, sir' from the previous page: 'You don't get to tell me no.' Brandon slips the blow and answers, 'I wasn't asking you for anything.'
Panel 2 — SMALL IMPACT PANEL. The pipe splinters a fence post. Marcus demands a fight; Brandon says plainly that he does not want one.

Panel 3 — MEDIUM ACTION. Marcus asks if Brandon is scared while swinging again. Brandon catches and redirects the arm into the wall: 'No. I just don't know you.' Keep it matter-of-fact rather than triumphant.

Panel 4 — REACTION WIDTH. Marcus shoves free, humiliated; one local behind him quietly lowers a hand that had been near a holster. Eva, already turned back to Tomas, tells Brandon that Tomas is breathing better.
Panel 5 — LARGER BOTTOM PANEL. Brandon turns his back on Marcus and kneels beside Tomas again, physically choosing the injured man over the contest. 'Good. Keep him on his side.'

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You don't get to tell me no.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't asking you for anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: No. I just don't know you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Good. Keep him on his side.

directionInline.text: Brandon's dry line should not turn the scene into a quip-fest. His real choice is physical: he returns to Tomas while Marcus still wants the audience.

title: Who Is Watching Whom
summary: Marcus discovers that the crowd's attention has shifted. One local helps Tomas without permission, weakening Marcus's control more than Brandon could have by defeating him.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM on a local woman stepping out of the crowd immediately after Brandon tells Eva to keep Tomas on his side. 'Move. I can help.' Eva reports that Tomas is breathing; the woman answers that she can see that and asks for the cloth.
Panel 2 — WIDER as Eva hands over the cloth and another local arrives with a fresh bucket. Marcus orders them to stay out of it. The woman replies, 'I was out of it. Then you hanged Tomas.'
Panel 3 — GROUND-LEVEL GROUP around Tomas. Brandon yields space and asks whether Tomas can sit up. The woman says not yet. Eva watches the locals begin helping without waiting for permission.
Panel 4 — ISOLATING MEDIUM on Marcus. He raises the pipe again, but now he is visually alone: 'This is my yard.' Tomas, weak but conscious, answers, 'I live here too.'

Panel 5 — LONG SHOT toward the road beyond the lot. Dust starts boiling into frame as Jessie's rig approaches fast; Marcus's claim of ownership is left hanging against the visible fact that the town has stopped obeying him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local woman
dialogueInline.text: I see that. Give me the cloth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local woman
dialogueInline.text: I was out of it. Then you hanged Tomas.

directionInline.text: This is consequence through community behavior, not a speech. Marcus loses some authority because people act independently while he is focused on the Brannock story.

title: The Rig
summary: Jessie drives into the back lot and turns the possibility of leaving into an immediate choice. Brandon makes sure Tomas is in local hands before moving.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — BIG ENTRANCE PANEL. Jessie's rig slews into the back lot through a low dust cloud. Her first word is Brandon's name; he answers the question she has not asked yet: 'He's breathing.'
Panel 2 — MEDIUM through the windshield. Jessie takes in Tomas, Marcus, Brandon and Eva in one sweep. 'Good. Get in.' Brandon asks for a minute; Jessie answers, 'No. Now.'

Panel 3 — SMALL REACTION TWO-SHOT on Eva and Jessie. Eva says Brandon really likes that minute; Jessie answers that she has noticed. The joke comes out of the repeated conversation rather than interrupting it.
Panel 4 — MEDIUM at Tomas. Brandon asks whether Tomas is all right with the people helping him. Tomas says yes and tells him to go. Brandon accepts the answer.

Panel 5 — WIDE EXIT BLOCK. Brandon stands and turns toward the rig. Marcus steps directly into the path and says, 'You're not walking out of here.' End on that obstruction so Page 18 can answer it immediately.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Tomas, are you all right with them?

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You're not walking out of here.

directionInline.text: Jessie does not rescue Brandon from a fight; she supplies motion. Brandon leaves only after another person has taken responsibility for Tomas.

title: Brandon Mack
summary: Marcus asks the question the whole issue has been circling. Brandon answers with his actual name and leaves Marcus to decide whether to believe it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM at the open passenger door. Marcus blocks Brandon's path after saying he is not walking out. Brandon answers simply, 'I am.' Marcus finally asks the question underneath every accusation: 'Who the hell are you?'
Panel 2 — CLOSE on Brandon. No dramatic lighting or identity effect: 'Brandon Mack.'
Panel 3 — REVERSE CLOSE on Marcus saying that is a lie. Brandon does not defend a biography; he only says, 'It's my name.'
Panel 4 — TWO-SHOT in profile. Marcus says Brannock ran once too. Brandon answers, 'Then ask him about it if he comes back.' Behind him Jessie calls his real name from the rig.

Panel 5 — WIDE as Marcus shifts just enough and Brandon walks past him. 'I'm coming' is directed to Jessie, not Marcus, making the exit part of the ongoing group conversation rather than a showdown button.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then ask him about it if he comes back.

directionInline.text: Do not play the last line as a cool-guy mic drop. Brandon is tired of the argument and genuinely means Marcus should save it for the person he wants.

title: The Third Passenger
summary: Brandon climbs into the rig and discovers Eva has already attached herself to the departure. Jessie refuses to stop long enough for Brandon to win the argument.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE MOVING SHOT. Brandon climbs into the passenger seat after telling Jessie he is coming. Jessie immediately starts rolling and tells him to shut the door before it is fully closed.
Panel 2 — MIRROR COMPOSITION. Brandon catches Eva on the rear step in the side mirror: 'Why is Eva on the rig?' Eva answers that she packed.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM THREE-QUARTER inside the rig as Brandon twists around: 'That wasn't my question.' Jessie cuts across the argument with the practical fact that they are moving.
Panel 4 — PROFILE TWO-SHOT Brandon/Jessie. Brandon appeals to Jessie by name; she tells him to argue while moving. He politely asks her to stop the rig. She says no.

Panel 5 — WIDER THREE-SHOT including Eva behind them. Brandon asks why moving is Jessie's answer to everything; Jessie says because it keeps working. Eva begins, 'Speaking of things that worked—' Brandon knows exactly where she is going and says, 'Don't.' End there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Why is Eva on the rig?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Why is moving your answer to everything?

directionInline.text: Eva's departure should feel opportunistic and prepared rather than fated. Jessie's refusal to stop is funny because it is also the practical reason Eva successfully joins them.

title: What He Heard
summary: Once the Last Drop is behind them, Eva reconstructs the first misidentification. Jessie called 'Brandon' from outside; the scarred patron heard 'Brannock' and then made the face fit the story he already knew.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LONG HORIZONTAL road panel. Eva answers Brandon's previous-page 'Don't' anyway: 'Brannock.' Brandon's resigned 'Of course' rides over the Last Drop shrinking behind them.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM inside the rig. Eva says Jessie called Brandon's name before he went inside. Jessie confirms it without turning from the road.

Panel 3 — MEMORY INSET with a soft-edged but non-mystical transition: Jessie at the rig calling 'Brandon' toward the saloon. Eva says the patron heard 'Brannock.' Brandon agrees that this explains the name.

Panel 4 — SECOND MEMORY INSET: the patron turns at the half-heard name; Brandon enters and the face completes the mistake. Eva says Brandon looked enough like whoever Brannock was; Jessie concludes that the patron filled in the rest.

Panel 5 — BACK IN THE RIG, three-shot. Eva expands the point: the patron did it first, then everyone else. Brandon says people have done worse with less. Eva answers, 'Not that fast.' End on the speed of belief, which Jessie answers on the next page.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Jessie called your name before you went inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then you walked in looking enough like whoever Brannock was.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: So he filled in the rest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: People have done worse with less.

directionInline.text: Do not sneak a mystery clue back into this page. Issue 1 works because the first identity can be explained completely as human error plus expectation. The larger pattern begins only when later cases stop fitting that explanation.

title: Careful Answers
summary: Eva and Jessie compare what the Brannock mistake revealed about Brandon and about the Last Drop while he can plainly hear them. Their theories about him become the first real conversation between the two women.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MOVING THREE-SHOT from the dashboard area. Jessie directly answers Eva's final 'Not that fast' from Page 20: 'That's the part I don't like.' Eva takes it as agreement; Jessie immediately narrows what she means.

Panel 2 — MEDIUM on Eva and Jessie, Brandon still present at frame edge. Eva points out that Jessie had Brandon's bag ready before the situation escalated. Jessie answers with the three men already outside waiting to 'remember' him.
Panel 3 — TIGHT on Eva refusing the dodge: 'That's not what I asked.' Jessie answers, 'I know.' The argument turns from Brannock to what Jessie thinks of Brandon.

Panel 4 — REVERSE on Jessie, eyes still on the road. Eva says Jessie trusts Brandon. Jessie gives the exact limit of that trust: what she has seen him do. Eva calls the answer careful; Jessie says she does not know him well enough to be careless.

Panel 5 — DEPTH COMPOSITION with Brandon foreground profile and the two women behind him. Brandon finally says he can still hear them. Eva uses that fact instead of apologizing: 'Good. Where are we going?' End on the question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That's the part I don't like.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I'm not agreeing with you. I'm agreeing that it was fast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You had his bag ready before it got that far.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: There were three men outside waiting to remember him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I trust what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough to be careless.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I can still hear both of you.

directionInline.text: This is the deliberate early Brandon-centered Eva/Jessie dialogue architecture. Their disagreement about what counts as evidence reveals how each woman thinks and creates the first intimacy between them.

title: Dust on the Lens
summary: The accidental trio continues into the Sunfields. Brandon remains himself; the Brannock mistake remains behind them but has already acquired a social life of its own, establishing both the group and the series engine without requiring a conspiracy.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE SUNFIELDS PANEL. Jessie answers Eva's previous-page question immediately: 'Away.' The rig passes a half-buried black Sunforge form being used by two workers to hold up shade cloth. Brandon replies that 'away' is not a place.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM inside the rig. Jessie says, 'It is from back there.' Eva opens a cheap notebook and writes BRANNOCK, then BRANDON MACK beneath it. No physical clue from the Last Drop is present.
Panel 3 — THREE-SHOT. Eva says away is good enough for her. Brandon's 'I was afraid you'd say that' is mild resignation, not rejection; the argument has become ordinary travel conversation.
Panel 4 — QUIET INTERIOR BEAT. For the first time the three simply ride together with no question demanding an answer. The first two closing captions sit over their ordinary shared silence.

Panel 5 — FINAL WIDE with a SMALL INSET. Main image: the rig is tiny against the Sunfields, three figures traveling together. Inset: back at the Last Drop, two locals retell the hanging to somebody who was not there. The final Brannock caption belongs over the inset.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I was afraid you'd say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By sundown, Brandon Mack is still a drifter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Back at the Last Drop, Brannock has already started traveling too.

directionInline.text: End on two simultaneous beginnings: the trio and the independent social life of the false identity. The Sunforge remains ordinary background texture. The narrator may create irony, but should not explain why any of this is happening.
